title: Stone Game II
summary: Alice and Bob alternate taking piles from the front.

contractDetails.output-checking: Exact typed equality of the returned int.

statement: Alice and Bob alternate taking piles from the front. Start with M=1. A turn may take X piles, where 1 ≤ X ≤ 2M and X does not exceed the number remaining. Then set M to max(M,X). Return the greatest total Alice can guarantee under optimal play.

examples.explanation: Alice can take both piles on the first move.
Taking one pile first lets Alice secure a total of 5 under optimal replies.

hints: Conceptual: The next player’s options depend on the number just taken.
Directional: A state needs the current position and M.
Implementation: Use suffix sums. For each legal X, subtract the opponent’s best total in the resulting state from all stones remaining in the current state.
complexityAnalysis: O(n³) time and O(n²) auxiliary space.
